captions.text: Recap of chapter 03: a class groups data with the functions that use it.
A dataclass writes the setup code for you.
Type hints describe your code, and your program can read them.
Inheritance lets different classes share one shape.
Today's black box: three features your framework depends on.
Let's open it.
First, flexible arguments. *args and **kwargs collect whatever is passed in.
Two stars also unpack a dictionary into named arguments.
This is how an agent runs a tool. The model sends arguments as a dictionary.
A decorator takes a function and returns a new one with extra behavior.
The wrapper does something extra, then calls the original function.
The @ sign applies it. Calling multiply now runs the wrapper first.
This decorator stores each function in a dictionary, then gives it back.
Adding @tool is all it takes. Your framework's tool system will work this way.
A generator uses yield to give back one value at a time, then pauses.
next gets one value, and list collects the rest.
Models stream their replies piece by piece, in just this way.
A context manager runs setup and cleanup around a block of code.
The with block runs at yield. finally always runs, even after an error.
Here, the block raises an error, and the cleanup still happens.
Now run it. Here are the flexible arguments and the decorator.
The registry found the tools by name, and the generator paused between words.
End risky work printed before the error was caught. Cleanup always runs.
This error means a decorator forgot to return its wrapper.
Your turn. Open exercises.py and complete the five TODOs.
You've finished when you see 5/5 passed.

points: Generators yield one at a time
